releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.11.0
releasesInRange.body:
This release adds Rust toolchain management, links the agent skills that dependencies ship, adds the `permissions` setting, and keeps the colors of streamed script output.

### Minor Changes

- `pnpm install` now links the agent skills that direct dependencies ship under `skills/<name>/SKILL.md` into the project's agent skill directories, such as `.claude/skills`. A package's skills are linked only after you approve them with `pnpm approve`. The `skills.dirs` setting chooses the directories [pnpm/rfcs#35](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/35).

  Added the `permissions` setting, which records what each dependency may do. Its `build` capability works like `allowBuilds` and takes precedence over it. `pnpm approve-builds` writes to `permissions` when `pnpm-workspace.yaml` already has it, and to `allowBuilds` otherwise.

  Added `pnpm permissions`, which lists the granted and denied permissions and the packages awaiting approval. `pnpm approve` reviews build scripts and agent skills in one prompt [pnpm/rfcs#36](https://github.com/pnpm/rfcs/pull/36).

- pnpm now installs and runs Rust toolchains.

  - With `cargo.enabled`, `pnpm install` installs the toolchain named in `rust-toolchain.toml`. pnpm verifies the release signature, stores the toolchain once per machine, and links it into `.pnpm/rust`. `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` put its `cargo` and `rustc` on the `PATH`.
  - `pnpm add -g rust@<channel>` installs a toolchain globally. The `cargo` and `rustc` commands run it outside projects that pin their own. `pnpm update -g`, `pnpm ls -g`, and `pnpm remove -g` manage it like any global package.
  - In a project, `pnpm add rust@<channel>` pins the toolchain in `rust-toolchain.toml`.
  - `pnpm shim add rust` adds project-aware shims for `cargo`, `rustc`, and the other Rust tools. In a project with a `rust-toolchain.toml`, they run the toolchain the file names and install it on first use. Elsewhere, the next command of the same name on `PATH` runs, such as rustup's.

- `pnpm run` and `pnpm exec` now keep the colors of script output that they print under the project's name, such as with `--stream`. pnpm sets `FORCE_COLOR=1` for these scripts when its own output is in color, unless `FORCE_COLOR` is already set.

  Script output is also rendered more cleanly:

  - A line that a progress bar redraws with `\r` shows only its last state.
  - Escape codes that move the cursor or clear the screen are dropped.
  - Long colored lines are cut at the terminal width.
  - `pnpm -r run` no longer garbles its live output when a script fails while other scripts are still running.

### Patch Changes

#### Installing packages

- pnpm no longer panics with "unexpected error when polling the I/O driver" when it runs under QEMU user-mode emulation, such as a `linux/amd64` container on an Apple Silicon Mac [#16696](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16696).

- `pnpm view`, `pnpm update`, and other commands that read registry metadata now work behind proxies that end a response by

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.11.1
releasesInRange.body: This release fixes two ways `pnpm install` could fail, runs tools of any Rust release through `pnx`, and treats `registry.npmjs.com` as an alias of the npm registry. ### Patch Changes - `pnpm install` no longer fails when `packageManager` pins the pnpm version that is already running and the registry does not publish that version. pnpm warns and continues. A registry mirror that has not synced a release no longer blocks the commands of a project pinned to it. - `pnpm install` no longer fails with `ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_CHMOD` when `node_modules/.bin` holds a shim that another user created, if everyone can already execute it and it is not world-writable. This happens when several users share one checkout. - `enable-modules-dir=false` (`enableModulesDir: false` through the Node.js addon) fetches the registry packages the host can install into the store again, as pnpm v10 did, while still writing nothing under `node_modules`. The setting exists for a `node_modules` that something else mounts from the store, such as a FUSE daemon, and that consumer no longer has to download each package on first access. A plain `--lockfile-only` run still fetches nothing. - `pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` no longer put `.npmignore` and `.gitignore` files in the tarball. A `files` entry that names one still ships it. - pnpm now treats `https://registry.npmjs.com/` as an alias of `https://registry.npmjs.org/`. Registry requests, credentials, and trusted publishing use the canonical hostname. - `pnx --package=rust@ ` runs a tool of that Rust release, for example `pnx --package=rust@nightly-2026-01-01 cargo build`. pnpm installs the release with the components and targets from `rust-toolchain.toml` and the target of each `--target` argument. - `pnpm install` now links agent skills for more coding agents. It detects the agent from `ANTIGRAVITY_AGENT`, `COPILOT_AGENT`, `COPILOT_CLI`, `CODEX_THREAD_ID`, `CODEX_SANDBOX`, `AI_AGENT`, and `CLAUDE_CODE` [pnpm/tasks#116](https://github.com/pnpm/tasks/issues/116). - When the registry rejects `pnpm stage publish`, the error message now starts with "Failed to stage package". ## Platinum Sponsors

releasesInRange.name: pnpm 12.12.0
releasesInRange.body:
This release shares task results and dependency builds through a remote cache, adds the `addMissingPeerTypes` setting, and lets `pnpm add --config` and `pnpm update` manage configuration dependencies. It also fixes `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` running the build scripts of packages that `allowBuilds` denies.

### Minor Changes

- `pnpm pipeline` can share task results between machines. A result is a signed artifact stored on a pnpr server or on a server that speaks the Turborepo Remote Cache API, such as Vercel Remote Cache.

  The remote side-effects cache can also store dependency builds on a Turborepo Remote Cache server. Both caches read the new `remoteCache` setting, which names the server and holds the signing keys. `pnpm pipeline --report` records the run under the organization `remoteCache.org` names.

- Added the `addMissingPeerTypes` setting, which links the `@types` package of a peer dependency next to every package that peer-depends on it. For example, a package that peer-depends on `react` gets the project's `@types/react` linked next to it. This lets TypeScript find the types of a peer dependency when the global virtual store is on [#15689](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/discussions/15689).

- `pnpm add --config` and `pnpm update` now handle configuration dependencies the way they handle other dependencies [#16814](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16814).

  `pnpm add --config` saves a version range in `pnpm-workspace.yaml` by the same rules as `pnpm add`, so `pnpm add --config my-config@latest` saves a range such as `^1.2.0`. It also resolves the package again when `pnpm-lock.yaml` already locks an older version.

  `pnpm update` updates configuration dependencies within their ranges, and `pnpm update --latest` moves them to their latest version. A selector such as `pnpm update my-config` updates only the configuration dependencies it names.

### Patch Changes

- A package set to `false` in `allowBuilds` no longer runs its build scripts when `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` is `true`. The two settings together now allow every build except the denied ones. Previously, `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds` ignored the denials.

- pnpm now switches to the pnpm version a project pins even when it cannot read its configuration. Previously, a setting it rejected in the global config file, an `.npmrc` file, or `_auth`, or a `pnpm-workspace.yaml` it could not parse, stopped every command, `pnpm --version` included.

- `pnpm update` and `pnpm why` accept `--depth Infinity` again. They failed with `invalid value 'Infinity' for '--depth <DEPTH>'` [#16817](https://github.com/pnpm/pnpm/issues/16817).

- `pnpm deploy` without `injectWorkspacePackages` now binds a peer dependency of a linked workspace package to the version its parent provides, as an injected install does. Previously the deploy failed with `ERR_PNPM_DEPLOY_AMBIGUOUS_PEER` whenever other packages in the deployed graph depended on different versions of that peer [#16807](https://github.com/pnpm/pn
…(truncated)

releasesInRange.body:
This release adds OIDC authentication to `pnpm dist-tag` and the `tool:` protocol. `pnpm publish` now checks which registry an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` was issued for before using it. ### Patch Changes - `pnpm publish` now uses an `NPM_ID_TOKEN` only if its `aud` claim matches the selected registry, such as `npm:registry.npmjs.org`. A token for another registry is skipped with a warning, and pnpm falls back to the configured credentials. - `pnpm dist-tag add`, `rm`, and `ls` now support OIDC authentication in CI. Enable "Allow npm dist-tag" in the package's trusted publishing settings to manage tags without a stored npm token. - Added the `tool:` protocol for the tools pnpm downloads itself: Node.js, Bun, Deno, and Yarn. `pnpm add bun@tool:1.3.0`, `pnx node@tool:22`, and `pnx yarn@tool:4` work like the `runtime:` spelling, which stays supported as an alias. A lockfile written for `runtime:` stays up to date when `package.json` switches to `tool:`, and the other way around. A named registry can no longer be called `tool`. ## Platinum Sponsors

prs.title: fix(pnpr): serve web UI assets completely when they are gzipped
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

pnpm/pnpm#16769 made pnpr stream web UI files. In a real browser the UI rendered blank: the scripts and styles failed with `ERR_INCOMPLETE_CHUNKED_ENCODING`. `curl --compressed` shows the response ending after the headers.

**Cause:** `streaming::stream_file` builds its body with `stream::unfold`, which panics when polled again after it ends. The gzip encoder in the compression layer does poll once more. Cached tarballs never hit this, because `application/octet-stream` is excluded from compression. UI assets are text, and big enough to be compressed. The existing UI tests used tiny files, which stay under the compression threshold.

**Fix:** both file streams in `streaming.rs` are fused. A new test fetches a 90 KB asset with `accept-encoding: gzip` and decodes it. It panics without the fix and passes with it.

The web UI has not been released yet, so there is no changeset.

prs.title: fix(pack): leave .npmignore and .gitignore out of the tarball
prs.author: incognitojam
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm pack` and `pnpm publish` in pnpm 12 put a package's `.npmignore` and `.gitignore` files into the tarball, at the root and in every subdirectory. pnpm 11 leaves them out, as npm does. No issue was filed for this.

Packing this package:

```
package.json   {"name":"fixture","version":"1.0.0"}
.npmignore     secret.txt
.gitignore     dist
index.js
lib/a.js
secret.txt
sub/.gitignore
sub/.npmignore
sub/b.js
```

11.28.5 packs `index.js`, `lib/a.js`, `package.json` and `sub/b.js`. 12.10.1 also packs `.gitignore`, `.npmignore`, `sub/.gitignore` and `sub/.npmignore`. The bug is pnpm 12 only, so the change is Rust only.

### Root cause

pnpm 11 uses npm-packlist, whose default rules start with `.npmignore` and `.gitignore`. Those unanchored patterns exclude both files at any depth. The Rust port in `pnpm-fs-packlist` keeps the rest of npm-packlist's defaults in `ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_BASENAMES`, `ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_DIR_SEGMENTS` and `ALWAYS_EXCLUDED_SUFFIXES`, but has no rule for the two ignore files. The walk reads them as ignore rules, and nothing then removes the files themselves.

npm-packlist's default rules are not absolute. A `files` entry is applied after them in the directory it matches, so an entry that matches an ignore file directly ships it. I checked this against 11.28.5:

| `files` | 11.28.5 packs |
| --- | --- |
| `[".npmignore", ".gitignore", "sub"]` | `.npmignore`, `.gitignore`, but not `sub/.npmignore` or `sub/.gitignore` |
| `[".*"]` or `["*"]` | `.npmigno

prs.title: fix(cmd-shim): skip chmod on a shim that is already executable
prs.author: adamwett
prs.body:
## Summary

When several users share one checkout (a shared test server, a group-writable deploy directory), every `pnpm install`, `pnpm add`, and every script run that triggers the pre-run install fails for everyone except the user who last wrote `node_modules/.bin`:

```
Error: ERR_PNPM_CMD_SHIM_CHMOD
  × installing dependencies
  ╰─▶ Failed to chmod "<project>/node_modules/.bin/biome": Operation not permitted (os error 1)
```

`write_shim` calls `set_executable` on the shim after deciding whether to rewrite it, including when the existing shim is already current. `Host::set_executable` replaced the mode with `0o755` unconditionally. On Unix only a file's owner may `chmod` it, even to its current mode, so a current, executable shim another user wrote fails the install. Group write access and setgid directories do not help.

pnpm v11 is not affected: `linkBin` returns early for a correctly linked bin and never chmods its shim. This is a v12-only fix.

The fix gives an existing shim the rule bin targets already follow in `ensure_executable_bits`: skip the chmod when every execute bit is already set. A world-writable shim is still reset to `0755`. A shim that lacks an execute bit is still chmodded, and that chmod still fails when the user does not own the shim. A shim the run has just created skips the probe and is chmodded directly, so a cold install does no extra `stat`.

## Squash Commit Body

```text
`write_shim` chmods the shim after every link, including when the shim on

prs.title: feat(pnx): run a tool of the Rust release --package=rust@<channel> names
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

With `cargo.enabled`, pnpm 12.11 puts the linked Rust toolchain on `PATH` in `pnpm run`. A script that needs another release, such as `cargo +nightly-2026-08-27 build`, then reaches the real cargo, which does not understand rustup's `+toolchain`. That broke the WebAssembly build in pnpm/pnpm#16781 (the pnpm 12.11 upgrade).

This PR adds a pnpm way to pick a release for one command, without taking over the `cargo` name:

```sh
pnx --package=rust@nightly-2026-08-27 cargo build --target wasm32-wasip1-threads
```

- `rust@<channel>` in `--package`, with one of the toolchain's tools as the command, is provisioned like `pnx node@22`. pnpm installs the release into the store and runs the tool from it, with its `bin` first on `PATH`. `RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN` is set to the toolchain directory so rustup's subcommand proxies run the same release.
- The release gets the profile, components, and targets of the toolchain file that governs the working directory, plus the target of each `--target` argument.
- A bare `rust` means `stable`. Anything that is not a channel, or a command that is not a toolchain tool, stays on the ordinary registry path.

Follow-up in pnpm/pnpm#16781 once this ships: the wasm and runtime-probe build scripts switch to `pnx --package=rust@nightly-… cargo`. The Dylint job is a separate script fix, because cargo-dylint calls the `rustup` binary itself.

prs.title: fix: keep installing when the packageManager pin names an unpublished running version
prs.author: KSXGitHub
prs.body:
## Summary

`pnpm install` fails outright when `packageManager` pins the pnpm version that is already running and the registry does not publish that version:

```
Error: ERR_PNPM_BAD_CONFIG_DEP
  x resolve package manager dependencies
  `-> Failed to resolve config dependency pnpm@12.11.0: No matching version
      found for pnpm@12.11.0 while fetching it from https://registry.npmjs.org/
```

A `packageManager` pin on pnpm 12 or newer persists, so the recording pass puts it under the env lockfile's `packageManagerDependencies` and resolves the pinned version from the registry to pin its bytes by integrity. A pin naming the running pnpm asks for no download, so when the registry does not serve that version there is nothing to record, and today that fails the whole command. Anyone on a registry mirror that has not synced a release yet, or on a build that is never published, has every command in a pinned project blocked by a pin on the pnpm they are already running.

It also makes `Build and run pnpm in WebContainers` red by construction after every release. That check pins the version the CLI it just built reports, so it cannot pass between the version bump landing on main and the packages being published. For 12.11.0 that window was 7h38m:

prs.author: zkochan

## Summary

Server side of signing in from pnpr's web UI (pnpm/tasks#113). The UI side shipped in `@pnpm/pnpr.apps.pnpr-web` 0.2.5, which `pnpr/ui` now builds. It adds a sign-in screen with a password form and one button per OIDC provider, sign-out, and keeps the token in the tab's `sessionStorage`.

- **`GET /-/pnpr/v0/sign-in`** lists the OIDC providers that offer browser sign-in, as `{"oidc": [{"name": ...}]}`.

prs.title: fix(package-manager): fetch into the store when the modules dir is disabled
prs.author: zkochan
prs.body:
## Summary

`enableModulesDir: false` (`enable-modules-dir=false`) exists for a `node_modules` that something else mounts from the store, such as a FUSE daemon. pnpm's TypeScript engine fetched every package into the store before it skipped the linking steps; the Rust engine treats the setting as `--lockfile-only` and fetches nothing, so the consumer of the mount downloads each package on first access, one at a time.

This restores the fetch. The run keeps the lockfile-only plumbing (no `node_modules`, no modules manifest, no workspace state) and fetches the lockfile's registry packages into the store: the frozen path from the wanted lockfile, through the tarball prefetcher, awaited; the fresh path through the resolver's tarball prefetch, which the run now turns on for this mode; it keeps the download tasks the prefetch spawns and waits on them, so a late or failed download is not missed. Index hits are checked by their files, since no materialization follows to repair a row whose files are gone, and an entry the install could not fetch fails the run. Packages the host cannot install (another platform's binaries) are left out, as the materialization leaves them out, and so are git and tarball-URL dependencies on the frozen path: they stay on the consumer's on-demand path, as every package was before. A plain `--lockfile-only` or `--dry-run` run still fetches nothing.

## Summary

With `dangerouslyAllowAllBuilds: true`, a package set to `false` in `allowBuilds` still ran its build scripts: `AllowBuildPolicy::check` returned `true` under the flag before looking at the denials. That left no way to say "build everything except these packages":

prs.author: zkochan

## Summary

Through the Node-API binding, a host can pass workspace projects in memory, with a `dependencyManifest` for the view an injected instance of a project gets (#13492). Resolution uses it. The checks that decide whether the lockfile can be reused did not, so every repeat install of such a workspace resolved again. On Bit's own workspace (342 projects, 259 of them with a `dependencyManifest`), a repeat install now reports "Already up to date" in under a second. Before, it resolved again on every run.

Three gaps, each confirmed on that workspace by logging which check rejected the lockfile:

1. **The injected project's manifest.** The repeat-install content check and the lockfile freshness check read an injected project's importer manifest instead of its `dependencyManifest`.
2. **`workspace:` dependencies of an injected project.** The check read the target's `package.json` from disk. Projects passed in memory may have none, so it now looks the target up among the loaded project manifests first.
3. **A dependency also declared as a peer.** The resolver lets the peer win when `autoInstallPeers` is on and the peer is not optional, or when the parent provides it (`peer_shadowed_dependencies`). The snapshot then records the peer, but the check compared it with the dependency's range. The check now mirrors the resolver. This one is not specific to the binding: any injected package that declares a name both ways was never judged fresh.

Adds the `addMissingPeerTypes` setting to pnpm v12. When it is on, every peer `X` of a dependency also makes `@types/X` an optional peer, unless the package already declares it. This is the rule Yarn applies in `normalizePackage`.

## Summary

Build output can now be shared between machines through one `remoteCache` setting. It covers both dependency side effects and `pnpm pipeline` task results, on either of two transports: a pnpr server, or a server that speaks the Turborepo Remote Cache API (Vercel Remote Cache or a self-hosted one).

The two caches now share one artifact format, one trust model, and one transport layer:

- **Format.** Pipeline task results are `workspace-task` artifacts of the shared artifact protocol. The protocol reserved that subject, but nothing used it until now. A task result is a signed P-256 envelope whose manifest mirrors a local cache entry (`meta.json` plus `outputs/`).
